name: og-00-vent-reactor-baseline
title: The Serpentinizing Vent
question: Can a Lost City-like, serpentinization-fed vent-ocean interface reproduce the physical and chemical environment in which the later origin-of-life steps are supposed to occur?
hypothesis: A 1D/2D porous-wall reactor with prescribed boundary fluxes reproduces published Lost City ranges (T, pH, H2, DIC) and qualitative precipitation trends while conserving mass and charge.
objective: Build a reduced vent–ocean reactor and validate it against Lost City field ranges to establish a geochemical/spatial testbed.
claim: Across the swept olivine-rate x flow-velocity grid, about 80% of the operating region falls inside the combined Lost City window (40-91 C, pH 9.0-10.8, positive H2 flux), and the baseline settles comfortably inside it at 50.6 C / pH 9.37 with sustained H2, exact charge balance, and spatial-flux divergence within tolerance. This establishes a bounded geochemical habitat, a region rather than a single tuned point, and makes no origin-of-life claim by itself.

findings.statement: Outlet settles at 50.6 °C and pH 9.37 — both inside the Lost City field window (40–91 °C, 9.0–10.8).
findings.explanation: Real PHREEQC peridotite serpentinization (Ca-OH endmember) + FiPy transport; pH is a genuine speciation result, not tuned.

findings.statement: Serpentinization delivers a sustained H2 reducing-power flux (min 2.75e-4 mol/s over the back half of the run).
PHREEQC charge balance is conserved exactly (|charge|=0) and the FiPy FVM spatial-flux divergence is held to 4.9e-5 — within the 1e-3 contract tolerance (not machine epsilon).
The Lost City pH endmember required reacting PERIDOTITE (olivine+pyroxene), not dunite — Ca released once Mg is consumed buffers the fluid to pH ~9.5.
findings.explanation: Olivine-only buffers at ~7.8 (brucite); adding diopside gives the Ca-OH endmember that reproduces field pH.

findings.statement: The vent wall convects. Solving Darcy–Boussinesq porous flow (a stream-function Poisson ∇²ψ = −buoyancy·∂T/∂x on the real FiPy mesh) gives a buoyant recirculation cell — the hot alkaline conduit rises, the cold ocean sinks, convective velocities ~5× the background upflow (Peclet ~8) — rather than a prescribed uniform upflow. The recirculation mixes cold ocean inward, settling the outlet ~8 °C cooler (59 → 51 °C) while staying inside the Lost City window; flux conservation is preserved within the solver tolerance (flux residual ~5e-5, within the 1e-3 bound).

evidence.observed: recirculation cell (cold-left sinks, hot-right rises); vmax ~5× background; outlet 50.6 °C

findings.explanation: FipyReactiveTransportProcess now solves the stream function each step and advects T + solute with the divergence-free Darcy velocity (u=∂ψ/∂y, v=−∂ψ/∂x + upflow); ψ contours are the streamlines the cross-section viz overlays. buoyancy=0 recovers the old constant upflow.

findings.statement: Habitability is a bounded REGION of the (olivine reaction rate × flow velocity) operating space, not one tuned run — the real PHREEQC + FiPy vent settles inside the Lost City window (T 40–91 °C AND pH 9.0–10.8 AND H2>0) over ~80% of the swept grid (115/144 points). The FAIL regions are a cold-washout band at the fastest flow (17 cold points) and 12 points at the flow extreme that fall outside PHREEQC's 0–100 °C validity (recorded NaN → FAIL); the baseline operating point sits safely inside the window.

evidence.observed: 115/144 (80%) habitable over (olivine_rate 0.005–0.4 × flow_velocity 2e-4–3e-2); 17 cold-washout FAILs, 12 out-of-range NaN; baseline (★) in-window at 50.6 °C / pH 9.37

findings.explanation: The vent_habitability_phase_map sweeps the real serpentinizing reactor and reduces each point to the habitability PASS flag (settled outlet in-window with a positive H2 flux); rendered as the Lost City habitability map (Decision view). Enough serpentinization to drive H2 + alkalinity and slow enough flow to hold 40–91 °C / pH 9.0–10.8 bounds the habitable band.
findings.next_action: Sweep pyroxene_fraction (ol/px ratio) and seawater-mixing dilution to bound the pH endmember (og-00b).

conclusion: The real PHREEQC + FiPy vent reactor reproduces the Lost City field window across a bounded ~80% habitability region of (olivine rate × flow velocity) and conserves mass/charge/flux at the baseline operating point, establishing the geochemical testbed og-01 builds on.

biological_validation.basis: No origin-of-life claim at this stage — this is a geochemical/spatial testbed only.

explanatory_gain.basis: Real speciation reproduces the field T/pH window AND reveals the peridotite Ca-OH endmember requirement — a mechanistic gain over the tuned box.

limitations: Heat-partition fraction calibrated to the observed vent temperature (chemistry otherwise emergent).
Single well-mixed interface; full 2-D chimney geometry deferred.

resolved_uncertainties: The Lost City high-pH endmember is the peridotite Ca-OH buffer (not the olivine brucite buffer).
Habitability is a bounded region (~80% of the olivine-rate × flow-velocity grid), not a single tuned point — the baseline sits inside it.

The habitability result is solver-robust — a FiPy↔FEniCS (dolfinx) head-to-head cross-check of the same spatial-transport face agrees on the vent (outlet T within 0.30%, identical pH, flux conserved ~1e-15), so the finding does not depend on the FiPy solver.
remaining_uncertainties: Sensitivity to the olivine/pyroxene ratio and to seawater-mixing dilution of the endmember.
The physical fate of the 12 flow-extreme points that exceed PHREEQC's 0–100 °C validity (currently FAIL by convention).

followup_study_proposals.rationale: Sweep pyroxene_fraction and mixing dilution to bound the pH endmember.

implemented_methods: Module A — REAL PHREEQC: genuine USGS IPhreeqc (via phreeqpython + vendored llnl.dat) reacting PERIDOTITE — olivine (forsterite+fayalite) + diopside pyroxene — with the serpentinite assemblage (chrysotile + brucite + magnetite + tremolite + diopside) each step. Dissolved H2, pH, pe, alkalinity and charge balance are emergent speciation outputs. The pyroxene-sourced Ca, once Mg is consumed into serpentine/brucite, gives the real Lost City Ca-OH-rich high-pH (~9.2-9.5) endmember — not a tuned value.

Module B — REAL FiPy: genuine finite-volume 1-D advection–diffusion–reaction column (TransientTerm == DiffusionTerm − PowerLawConvectionTerm, scipy direct-LU solve, zero-gradient advective outflow BC) transporting the serpentinization source across the vent–ocean interface.

Partial-equilibrium coupling: a flow/temperature kinetic driver sets the olivine reaction extent feeding the equilibrium speciation (standard reactive-transport practice). The only field-calibrated knob is the heat-partition fraction (tuned to the observed 40–91 C vent temperature); all chemistry is emergent.

Conservation: PHREEQC conserves elements + charge by construction; FiPy's FVM conserves flux to the linear-solver tolerance (residual ~5e-5, within the 1e-3 bound) — directly satisfying the mass_balance / charge_neutrality / spatial_flux_conservation contract invariants.

contract.note: bigraph-schema typed ports (_type/_units/bounds) + conservation predicates; the composite built for this study must declare a ProcessContract matching this face (audited via the workbench §Contract panel).

behavior_tests.name: vent-pH-in-lostcity-range
behavior_tests.description: Settled outlet pH sits in the Lost City envelope (9.0-10.8). Met by reacting PERIDOTITE (olivine + diopside pyroxene), not dunite: once Mg is consumed into serpentine/brucite, the Ca released from pyroxene gives the real Ca-OH-rich, high-pH endmember (tremolite/diopside-buffered), reproducing field pH ~9.2-9.5 at vent temperature — a genuine PHREEQC speciation result, not a tuned value.

literature_anchors.expectation: Lost City ~40-91 C, pH ~9-10.8, >=30 ky activity
literature_anchors.status_in_workspace: Met by the real coupled model: settled T ~51 C and pH ~9.4 are both in the Lost City window, H2 reducing power is sustained, and mass/charge/flux conservation hold. pH was closed by reacting peridotite (olivine + pyroxene) so the Ca-OH endmember buffers the fluid to field pH — a real PHREEQC result.

key_assumptions: Hadean ocean chemistry parameterized separately — never reuse modern seawater as the ancient prior.

Partial equilibrium: a prescribed olivine dissolution rate (flow/T-driven) feeds PHREEQC equilibrium speciation each step — fast aqueous/mineral equilibrium vs a rate-limited rock reaction, standard for reactive-transport.

The heat-partition fraction (fraction of serpentinization enthalpy retained in the fluid parcel) is CALIBRATED to the observed 40-91 C vent temperature; the chemistry (H2, pH, pe, charge) is emergent from PHREEQC, not tuned.
expert_questions: Reproduce Lost City (modern analog) and parameterize Hadean ocean separately, or attempt a Hadean-only baseline first?

pH endmember (RESOLVED): reacting peridotite (olivine + diopside pyroxene) with the serpentinite+tremolite assemblage drives the Mg-depleted Ca-OH fluid to field pH ~9.2-9.5 at vent T. Open follow-up: sensitivity to pyroxene_fraction (ol/px ratio) and to seawater-mixing dilution of the endmember.
